chunks: Harith ibn al-Mughirah al-Nadri narrated from Abi Abd Allah عليه السلام that he said:

Whoever hears the mu'adhdhin say, 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,' then says, affirming and seeking reward, 'And I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. I suffice with these two against everyone who refuses and rejects, and I support with them everyone who affirms and bears witness,' there shall be for him, of reward, the number of those who deny and reject and the number of those who affirm and bear witness.

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ: I bear witness; a formal declaration of testimony and conviction
key_terms.أَكْتَفِي: I suffice myself; I rely upon these two testimonies
key_terms.الْأَجْرِ: the divine reward granted for this response
key_terms.الْمُؤَذِّنَ: the caller to prayer who proclaims the adhān
key_terms.مُحْتَسِبًا: seeking reward from Allah with sincere intention
key_terms.مُصَدِّقًا: affirming the truthfulness of what is being proclaimed

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for repeating the shahādah after hearing the mu'adhdhin?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the merit of responding to the adhān by repeating the two testimonies with sincere affirmation and hope for divine reward. It presents the shahādah as both a declaration of tawhid and risālah and a means of aligning oneself with those who accept the truth, bringing immense reward.
